title: Roots of the Vietnam War Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll trace Vietnam from French colony to the 1954 partition.
meta_desc: GCSE OCR History — French Indochina, Dien Bien Phu and Geneva 1954.
final_note: You learned how French defeat split Vietnam at the 17th parallel.

concepts.def: Colony of Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia from 1887
1954 French military disaster in north-west Vietnam
Eisenhower fear that Asia would fall to communism

walkthroughs.body_html:
France ruled Indochina from 1887, growing rubber and rice.

Ho Chi Minh founded the Indochinese Communist Party in 1930 and led the Viet Minh from 1941. He declared independence on 2 September 1945 — but France returned to crush it.

From 1946 the First Indochina War dragged on. The US paid 80% of French costs.

At Dien Bien Phu in 1954 General Giap's troops surrounded the French. France surrendered after 56 days — losing 11,000 prisoners.

The 1954 Geneva Accords split Vietnam at the 17th parallel.

Ho's communists held the North; Ngo Dinh Diem ran the Catholic South. Elections were due in 1956 but Diem refused. Eisenhower warned of falling dominoes if the South collapsed.
